html:
The German protectorate over Cameroon, which began when the Duala kings of the Cameroon estuary signed a treaty with German traders in July 1884, and the envoy Gustav Nachtigal raised the flag.

Germany then pushed inland for three decades, fighting many peoples, and in the Scramble for Africa stretched the colony to Lake Chad. Plantations on the slopes of Mount Cameroon used forced labour, and the Germans built roads, railways and the port of Douala. Their seizure of Duala land led to the execution of Rudolf Duala Manga Bell. German rule ended in the Kamerun campaign of 1914 to 1916, and the land was split between France and Britain. See also Kamerun.
